races.name: Ladies Day Sunday 16th August Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Limerick Leader
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 278-day break with stamina questions at 3m but gets uncontested lead
runners_data.comment: In good form in early part of last season; Sean Bowen booked for stable debut; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: In good form for Alison Thorpe in early part of last season, notably when winning at Newton Abbot (2m5f, good); yet fully to convince stamina-wise at around 3m and has fitness to prove on this stable debut (same owners) but Sean Bowen (who has won on him before) is booked; swaps visor for first-time blinkers.

runners_data.name: Anytrixwilldo
runners_data.note: Prominent runner wearing first-time blinkers after disappointing last time, needs to bounce back
runners_data.spotlight: 1-15 over fences; runner-up twice in cheekpieces at Ludlow (3m, good to soft) at start of this year but didn't fire in first-time blinkers (retained) at Fontwell last month; others are more persuasive.

runners_data.name: No More No
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from 13-month absence but has winning C&D form over fences
runners_data.comment: Absent since 31l win over C&D on chase debut last May, but that also came after a layoff
runners_data.spotlight: Won over hurdles here in October 2024 and returned from seven-month break with wide-margin C&D (good) success on chasing debut last May; absent for another 13 months since and now 13lb higher but remains unexposed over fences and can evidently go well when fresh.

runners_data.name: Another Mystery
runners_data.note: Prominent type with victory at Fakenham but hard to assess true ability from weak opposition
runners_data.comment: Finished alone at Fakenham in April; the form is hard to weigh up but the time was good
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to racing under rules with win in four-runner chase at Fakenham (3m, good) in April, in which his three rivals toiled and were pulled up; it's hard to gauge what that form is worth and his overall profile is not compelling but he clocked a good time (despite being eased right down).

runners_data.name: Wings On Wheels
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse still unexposed under rules, cheekpieces helped last time at Huntingdon
runners_data.comment: Still unexposed under rules but needs improvement over this new trip
runners_data.spotlight: Still unexposed under rules and was seemingly aided by new cheekpieces when second of four at Huntingdon (2m4f, good) in March; that form isn't anything to get excited about, though, and he was well held when third at Perth (2m4f, good to soft) last month; needs improvement over this new trip.

runners_data.name: Pleasure Garden
runners_data.note: Prominent runner effectively 7lb higher in weights, recent fourth suggests current form level
runners_data.comment: Gained only chase win in 2023 and is 9lb wrong here; tries a new trip
runners_data.spotlight: Ran well for a long way before fading into fourth at Huntingdon (2m4f, good) last month but is effectively 7lb higher from out of the weights here and it's over three years since his only chase win; tries a new trip.

runners_data.name: Friends Don't Ask
runners_data.note: Prominent veteran with recent placed form, lost by short head at Fontwell last month
runners_data.comment: Back from break with three placed runs last month; can make presence felt again
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time chase winner; no longer the force of old but returned from break with three placed runs last month, losing out only by a short head at Fontwell (3m2f, good) last time; can make his presence felt again.

runners_data.name: Milan Milos
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who made winning chase debut in tongue-tie, stepping up significantly in class
runners_data.comment: Battled on well to make winning chase debut at Plumpton; still unexposed as a stayer
runners_data.spotlight: 0-8 over hurdles but battled on well to make winning chase debut in four-runner contest at Plumpton (3m1f, good; first-time tongue-tie) in April and was nudged up only 2lb for that; remains unexposed beyond 2m4f; no surprise if he features.

runners_data.name: Huckleberry Sting
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who races too freely but showed marked improvement when upped to 3m
runners_data.comment: Won when upped to 3m on chase debut in April and not discredited here last time
runners_data.spotlight: Low-mileage 7yo who tends to race too freely but displayed considerable improvement when upped to 3m and switched to fences at Bangor (good) in April, winning by 5l; beaten about 21l when second over C&D last month but gave the all-the-way winner far too much rope that day, and his margin of defeat was magnified by late jumping errors; remains of strong interest.

races.paceDynamic: Limerick Leader will dictate terms from the front with no genuine pace pressure, allowing him to bowl along comfortably. The prominent brigade of Anytrixwilldo, Another Mystery, Pleasure Garden and Friends Don't Ask will create congestion behind the leader, particularly dangerous approaching the business end where traffic problems could emerge. Hold-up horses No More No, Wings On Wheels, Milan Milos and Huckleberry Sting face the challenge of navigating through this congested pack from off the pace. This sustained gallop strongly favours the front-running Limerick Leader and those who can secure clean runs from prominent positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Limerick Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Limerick Leader maintains his jumping rhythm and isn't pressured for the lead
scenarios.body: The confirmed front-runner gets his preferred uncontested lead and kicks clear approaching two out, with the prominent horses struggling to close the gap. His stamina concerns are negated by the controlled pace he sets himself.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent runners create interference and bunch up turning for home
scenarios.body: The congested pack behind Limerick Leader allows a hold-up horse with racing room to sweep through late. No More No or Milan Milos benefit from the pace collapse and clean passage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Another Mystery Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Another Mystery can secure the best prominent position without traffic issues
scenarios.body: The lightly-raced 9-year-old uses his Fakenham win momentum to track Limerick Leader cleanly and outstay him in the final furlong. His fresh legs from limited recent racing tell against more exposed rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closing Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly run and multiple horses stay on strongly
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop sets up a proper staying test where class horses like No More No and Huckleberry Sting can use their ability. The race becomes a genuine stamina examination rather than a tactical affair.

watchPoints.text: Limerick Leader faces first run in 278 days at a trip where his stamina is questioned - fitness could tell late
Anytrixwilldo sports first-time blinkers after poor Fontwell run - headgear change suggests connections concerned
Traffic problems highly likely between Anytrixwilldo, Another Mystery, Pleasure Garden and Friends Don't Ask in prominent positions
No More No returns from 393-day break but has winning C&D form when fresh - market support would be telling
Another Mystery's Fakenham win came against weak opposition where three rivals were pulled up - form needs upgrading

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Electric Eddy
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid chase form but inconsistent record, Twiston-Davies yard struggling with 0/8 record in last 14 days
runners_data.comment: Good second on chase debut in November but below that form twice since; others preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Kept on well for second on chase debut at Hereford (2m, good) in November but was pulled up on next outing and made low-key reappearance when third of five (probably only fourth best on merit) at Worcester (2m, good) last month; needs to up his game here.

runners_data.name: Catchim
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who needs to avoid going too fast early, recent Market Rasen win came when left clear shows vulnerability to pressure
runners_data.comment: Left clear to open chase account at Market Rasen in April; well beaten there since
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who was left clear just after final fence to score at Market Rasen (2m1f, good) in April, opening his chase account at the 12th attempt, but needs to bounce back quickly from a poor run there 12 days ago.

runners_data.name: Alshadhian
runners_data.note: Last year's winner returning after 236-day break, class horse but fitness major concern after eight months off
runners_data.comment: Won this in 2025 but has fitness to prove after 236-day break and is on fairly tough mark
runners_data.spotlight: Won this race by 13l a year ago and was still in good form when last seen last summer/autumn; has fitness to prove after eight-month absence, though, and current mark probably demands a career-best performance.

runners_data.name: Kill The Groove
runners_data.note: Prominent runner now 9lb lower in weights but disappointing chase form this spring suggests limited improvement
runners_data.comment: Well handicapped on hurdle second in January but safely held in both chases this spring
runners_data.spotlight: Now 9lb lower than when going close over hurdles at Plumpton (2m, soft) in January but was safely held in both chases this spring (2m3f/2m), and cheekpieces didn't appear to help much when used once previously.

runners_data.name: Beorma
runners_data.note: Fast-improving mare with excellent recent form, won chasing debut easily 6 days ago and Skelton yard firing at 14/27
runners_data.spotlight: Fast-improving mare who won easily on chasing debut at Worcester (2m, good; first-time tongue-tie) 12 days ago and has quickly added two easy hurdle wins (2m4f/2m, good) to her tally; probably still a long way ahead of the handicapper and can continue her winning spree here.

runners_data.name: Walk The Plank
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs a strong pace to be effective, recent form solid but lowest official rating creates tough task
runners_data.comment: Battled well to win at Huntingdon in March and also ran well 12 days ago; place claims
runners_data.spotlight: Battled well for narrow success at Huntingdon (2m, good) in March, his third chase start, and gave another good account before fading into fourth at Market Rasen (2m1f, good) 12 days ago; might collect a minor prize.

runners_data.name: Fond Farewell
runners_data.note: Struggles in hurdles for current connections, making chasing debut but limited evidence of ability at this level
runners_data.comment: Not beaten far over hurdles recently but not bred for chasing; others are much safer
runners_data.spotlight: Won a low-grade Flat handicap in Ireland in 2023 but unplaced all six hurdle runs for current stable; not beaten far when fifth of six at Worcester (2m, good) recently but not bred for chasing; others are much safer.

races.paceDynamic: Catchim is the lone confirmed front-runner and will likely dictate terms from the start, setting a sustainable pace without early pressure in this small field. Electric Eddy, Alshadhian, Kill The Groove, and Beorma will likely track within 3-4 lengths as prominent runners, while Walk The Plank and Fond Farewell settle further back. The lack of pace pressure should see Catchim still there turning for home, but the moderate gallop will play into the hands of the prominent runners who can quicken from close range. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can track the leader and kick clear from the final fence.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Catchim Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Catchim gets an easy lead and jumps cleanly through the race.
scenarios.body: The front-runner's stamina and jumping will prove decisive when others try to quicken, as he's proven he can win when getting his own way. His recent Market Rasen success came in exactly these conditions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Kick Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays moderate and multiple horses are still in contention at the last fence.
scenarios.body: Beorma or Electric Eddy will have the tactical advantage to strike from close range, using their class edge over the front-runner. The sustainable gallop will set up perfectly for a sharp injection of pace late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes stronger than expected or Catchim goes too fast.
scenarios.body: Walk The Plank's proven stamina will allow him to pick up the pieces as prominent runners tire, similar to his Huntingdon success. The extended sprint will suit his patient style perfectly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Alshadhian Returns Strong
scenarios.trigger: If the defending champion shows no signs of his eight-month absence.
scenarios.body: His class advantage and course knowledge will overcome any fitness concerns, as he dominated this race by 13 lengths last year. The moderate pace will mask any conditioning shortfall.

watchPoints.text: Watch Catchim's jumping under pressure - if others close up turning for home his technique could deteriorate as seen in previous defeats
Monitor Alshadhian's fitness signs early - any laboured jumping or struggling to maintain position will confirm the long absence has left its mark
Check if Beorma shows any signs of her rapid recent campaign catching up, particularly her jumping fluency after just 6 days since debut chase win
Observe Walk The Plank's position turning in - needs to be within 6-8 lengths to have any realistic chance in this company
Watch for any early pace pressure on Catchim from the prominent runners, which could set up the race for hold-up horses

races.name: Southwell Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Nazare
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 30 days off with disappointing recent chase form but has winning hurdles experience at this track
runners_data.comment: Has lost way since his two hurdle wins in November; well held when third on chase debut
runners_data.spotlight: Lost his way after winning twice over hurdles in November (2m4f, good to soft; once here) and was a disappointing favourite when well-held third of four on last month's chasing debut at Ludlow (3m, good); may yet turn things around but comes here with quite a bit to prove.

runners_data.name: Manowest
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner making chasing debut for in-form Olly Murphy but poor recent hurdles form is concerning despite Irish point win
runners_data.comment: Just 1-12 over hurdles and disappointed last time but makes chase debut from workable mark
runners_data.spotlight: Just 1-12 over hurdles and ran poorly when upped to 3m2f at Perth last month; makes chasing debut from a workable mark, though, and his Irish point win in 2024 bodes well for his prospects over fences.

runners_data.name: Thank You Blue
runners_data.note: Natural front runner who completed hat-trick over hurdles but form tailed off badly towards end of last season, 53 days off
runners_data.comment: Won three hurdles in February but quickly went off boil afterwards; risky on chase return
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to form and completed quick hat-trick over hurdles in February (2m-2m4f, good to soft/soft) but quickly went off the boil towards end of last season (pulled up on two of last three appearances); competes off his lower chase mark here and might be allowed an uncontested lead but has a poor completion rate over fences; risky.

runners_data.name: Cher Monsieur
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with recent chase win at Plumpton, carries top weight but wears cheekpieces and has tactical pace advantage
runners_data.comment: Raised only 3lb for recent Plumpton win and probably still on the upgrade; good chance
runners_data.spotlight: Scored over hurdles at start of this year and built upon his promising chase debut when winning four-runner race at Plumpton (2m4f, good) a fortnight ago; only 3lb higher here and probably still on the upgrade; wears tongue-tie for first time; good chance.

races.paceDynamic: Thank You Blue is the lone front runner and will be allowed to dictate terms at his own pace without pressure. Nazare, Manowest and Cher Monsieur all prefer to come from behind, creating a tactical mismatch where the leader faces minimal early harassment. With three hold-up/prominent runners bunched behind an uncontested pacesetter, the race sets up perfectly for those tracking the pace to time their challenge. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners like Cher Monsieur who can sit close enough to strike when Thank You Blue inevitably comes back to them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Thank You Blue maintains his recent hurdles form and gets an easy lead
scenarios.body: The 9-year-old can dictate fractions and kick clear at the business end when rivals are still organising their challenges. His hat-trick over hurdles in February proves he has the engine when allowed to control proceedings.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Cher Monsieur can sit second or third behind the easy pace
scenarios.body: The improving chaser can travel smoothly in Thank You Blue's slipstream before unleashing his proven finishing kick in the final furlong. His recent Plumpton win shows he's learning the chasing game quickly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Nazare or Manowest could benefit from a truly-run race where their stamina kicks in late. The distance and good ground would suit both if they can overcome their recent poor form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Thank You Blue stops quickly and no one else can sustain a challenge
scenarios.body: A messy finish where positioning luck and jumping accuracy become crucial factors. The race could fall apart with tired horses making errors at the business end.

watchPoints.text: Thank You Blue's jumping accuracy on chasing return after 53 days off - any early mistakes could end his chances quickly
Nazare's fitness levels after 30-day break following disappointing last run where he was well-held as favourite
Manowest's chasing debut tactics with Sean Bowen aboard - will need to adapt quickly from hurdles style
Cher Monsieur carrying top weight at 152lbs but has tactical advantage sitting behind uncontested leader
Early pace development - if Thank You Blue doesn't lead immediately, the race dynamic changes completely

races.name: Ladies Day Sunday 16th August Maiden Hurdle (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Trigger The Light
runners_data.note: Front runner returning from 221-day break but should get uncontested lead with sustainable pace
runners_data.comment: Third in a bumper in October but pulled up on hurdle debut; had wind op during layoff
runners_data.spotlight: Made quite promising rules debut when third in seven-runner Warwick bumper (good) in October but was pulled up on hurdling debut later that month (2m4f, good to soft); had wind op during seven-month break.

runners_data.name: Run Happy
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with most recent form, likely to track the pace and threaten late
runners_data.comment: Fifth of 14 in pointers' bumper on rules debut at Aintree; improvement needed here
runners_data.spotlight: Made quite promising rules debut when fifth of 14 in pointers' bumper at Aintree (good) last month but almost certainly needs to improve to threaten the principals on this hurdling debut.

runners_data.name: Manalishi
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with consistent placed form but faces traffic concerns from wide draw
runners_data.comment: Placed all three hurdling starts, most recently when clear second at Uttoxeter last month
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up on last year's bumper debut and placed on all three hurdling starts, most recently when clear second of eight at Uttoxeter (2m4f, good) last month; leading contender.

runners_data.name: Hawk's Rock
runners_data.note: Irish raider running prominently with cheekpieces, recent form suggests improvement trajectory
runners_data.comment: Launched hurdling career with two promising runs last month; in the mix again here
runners_data.spotlight: Irish raider who launched hurdling career with two promising runs in cheekpieces last month, latterly when close fourth of ten at Cartmel (2m6f, good); that form already puts him on the premises here, and he can improve if he cuts out the jumping errors.

runners_data.name: Who's Glen
runners_data.note: Quality hold-up performer but 69-day break and needs significant pace collapse to be effective
runners_data.comment: Placed in valuable series final in March and ought to play a significant role in this.
runners_data.spotlight: Useful Flat racer who made the frame on four of his five hurdling starts for Donald McCain last season, most notably when third in valuable series final at Musselburgh (2m4f, good to soft) in March; well beaten in good-quality Flat handicap last month but ought to play a significant role in this.

runners_data.name: Rock Sensation
runners_data.note: Course winner as hold-up horse but inconsistent hurdling form, wears tongue tie
runners_data.comment: Looked quite useful in bumpers but has made underwhelming start to hurdling career
runners_data.spotlight: Won good-ground course bumper for Ben Pauling in spring 2025 and made the frame in soft-ground Listed bumper at Cheltenham in November but has made an underwhelming start to her hurdling career; shaped with some promise on last month's stable debut at Fontwell (2m1f, good) but was safely held in the end; needs to up her game over this longer trip.

runners_data.name: Papillondelumiere
runners_data.note: Prominent but limited ability, 8-year-old maiden wearing tongue tie shows desperation
runners_data.comment: Maiden pointer who was soundly beaten when 100-1 for first two hurdling starts
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden pointer who was soundly beaten when 100-1 for first two hurdling starts.

runners_data.name: Granite Sands
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse improving but needs major step forward, headgear applied suggests issues
runners_data.comment: Second hurdle run was better than the debut but another big step forward is needed
runners_data.spotlight: Bettered low-key hurdle debut when keeping on for modest third of six at Stratford (2m6f, good to firm) last month but needs to take another good step forward here.

runners_data.name: Jacquette
runners_data.note: Weak hold-up performer switching yards, completely out of her depth at this level
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at huge odds on both hurdling starts for Danni O'Neill; now with new stable
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten at huge odds on both hurdling starts for Danni O'Neill; now with Georgie Howell.

races.paceDynamic: Trigger The Light is the confirmed front runner but shouldn't face pressure from the prominent runners Run Happy, Hawk's Rock and Papillondelumiere who are unlikely to be aggressive early. The large contingent of hold-up horses (Manalishi, Who's Glen, Rock Sensation, Granite Sands, Jacquette) will likely settle towards the rear allowing a comfortable tempo. This creates a tactical setup where the pace-setters can dictate without early pressure, then the hold-up brigade will need to find gaps and momentum late over this stamina-testing 2m4½f trip. This race shape strongly favours the prominent runners who can track the pace and have first run on the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace stays manageable as expected with minimal pressure on Trigger The Light
scenarios.body: The prominent contingent of Trigger The Light, Run Happy and Hawk's Rock can position perfectly and have first run on the large hold-up brigade who face traffic problems late. The stamina test of 2m4½f plays to horses who don't have to make up significant ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finds Gap
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses gets a clear run and benefits from a strong pace collapse
scenarios.body: Manalishi or Who's Glen could capitalise on their superior ratings if the pace becomes unsustainable and the leaders weaken significantly up the straight. The class edge of these proven performers shows through late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Trigger Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Trigger The Light gets an uncontested lead and maintains stamina to the line
scenarios.body: With no genuine pace pressure early, Trigger The Light could steal a march and prove hard to peg back despite limited experience, similar to many front-running maiden hurdle winners. The long absence becomes less relevant if unopposed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Benefits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses encounter significant traffic problems allowing a bigger-priced runner through
scenarios.body: Rock Sensation or Granite Sands could benefit from a chaotic finish where the fancied hold-up horses are trapped behind faltering leaders. Previous course experience gives Rock Sensation a small edge in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic problems affecting the large hold-up contingent of Manalishi, Who's Glen, Rock Sensation if they're all converging late
Monitor Trigger The Light's fitness on comeback from 221-day layoff - any signs of rustiness could open door
Observe if Hawk's Rock's cheekpieces continue to spark improvement following promising Irish form
Check if the pace becomes genuinely strong - current setup suggests comfortable tempo that may not suit hold-up horses
Watch Rock Sensation's jumping under pressure given inconsistent hurdling record despite course bumper win

races.name: Vaughandale Construction 'Built To Last' Novices' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Phantom Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning to handicaps after bumper success, benefits from patient ride and sustained pace
runners_data.comment: Did not get competitive in three maiden/novice hurdles; may do better in handicaps, though
runners_data.spotlight: Did not get competitive in three maiden/novice hurdles (2m-2m4f) for new stable this spring, following a long absence, but won a bumper by 9l in summer 2023 and there's still a chance some of that ability will resurface at some point; watch the betting.

runners_data.name: Collanisi
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form, solid recent third suggests ready to strike in this grade
runners_data.comment: Made solid start to handicap hurdle career when third at Uttoxeter last month; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Made solid start to handicap career when close third of eight at Uttoxeter (2m, good) last month and any improvement on that performance will give him a good shout here.

runners_data.name: Paragon
runners_data.note: Forward-going type wearing cheekpieces, recent fourth at Market Rasen shows competitive handicap form
runners_data.comment: First two handicap runs were respectable but he needs to find something extra today
runners_data.spotlight: Made fairly encouraging handicap debut over C&D (good) last month and his recent fourth in first-time cheekpieces at Market Rasen (2m, good) was also respectable; needs to find something extra today, though.

runners_data.name: Global Hideaway
runners_data.note: Lone pace-setter returning after 357-day absence, previous bleeding issues raise fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: Pulled up when making handicap debut for Dan Skelton; makes stable debut after layoff
runners_data.spotlight: Bled from the nose on final two starts for Dan Skelton, latterly when pulled-up 66-1 shot on handicap debut just under a year ago; now with Christian Williams (same owner); others have much less to prove.

runners_data.name: Caspada
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with scope for improvement, 150-1 second at Chepstow suggests untapped potential
runners_data.comment: Belied big odds when second in 14-runner Chepstow maiden in April; handicap debut today
runners_data.spotlight: Soundly beaten on first two hurdling starts but belied 150-1 odds when second in 14-runner Chepstow maiden (2m, good) in April and has plenty of scope for further improvement in handicaps.

runners_data.name: Brooklyn Lullaby
runners_data.note: Patient type resuming after 255-day break, minimal form suggests needs significant improvement
runners_data.comment: Showed no significant promise when a big-priced outsider for three maiden hurdles in 2025
runners_data.spotlight: Showed no significant promise when a big-priced outsider for three maiden hurdles last August/September and makes handicap debut after a 255-day absence; 2lb wrong; of interest only if attracting market support.

runners_data.name: Prettylady
runners_data.comment: Displayed improvement to win on last month's handicap hurdle debut; can progress again
runners_data.spotlight: Made low-key start to British hurdling career last season but delivered on promise shown on the Flat in France when winning from off the pace on last month's handicap hurdle debut at Stratford (2m, good to firm); could easily have more improvement to come.

runners_data.name: Versatile
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with frame placings, claiming jockey suggests connections confident
runners_data.comment: Showed promise when making the frame on first two hurdling starts; needs improvement here
runners_data.spotlight: Displayed promise when making the frame in two maiden hurdles (2m, good/good to firm) this spring but he refused to race on the Flat in between and needs to improve to overcome top weight on this handicap hurdle debut.

runners_data.name: Red Trail
runners_data.note: Patient performer now 0-15 over hurdles, limited profile despite recent Paragon form line
runners_data.comment: Not disgraced at Market Rasen recently but now 0-15 over hurdles; others are much stronger
runners_data.spotlight: Not disgraced when fifth of seven (behind Paragon) at Market Rasen (2m, good) 12 days ago, after a break, but is now 0-15 over hurdles and her overall profile is not appealing.

runners_data.name: Beaufort Breeze
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning after 524-day absence, fading tendency creates concerns
runners_data.comment: Absent since three low-key qualifying runs in 2024-25 season; still worth a market glance
runners_data.spotlight: Irish point winner in spring 2024; well beaten at triple-digit odds in three novice/maiden hurdles in 2024-25 season (2m-2m4f) but two of those were good-quality races at Cheltenham; makes handicap debut after a long absence but remains unexposed and is worth a glance in the betting.

runners_data.name: Littletown Lad
runners_data.note: Free-going hold-up horse with finishing problems, tendency to race keenly remains issue
runners_data.comment: Unable to justify prominence in the betting when soundly beaten in first two handicaps
runners_data.spotlight: Unable to justify prominence in the betting when soundly beaten in first two handicaps, the latter over C&D last month, and his tendency to race too freely remains a worry; evidently thought capable of better, though.

races.paceDynamic: Global Hideaway stands alone as the confirmed front runner and will dictate proceedings from flag-fall without pressure, likely setting a steady, sustainable gallop over this 2-mile trip. Collanisi and Paragon both show prominent tendencies but neither is compelled to challenge Global Hideaway early, meaning the pace will be controlled rather than testing. This creates a tactical race where the early tempo suits patient types, with the real race beginning from the final 3-4 furlongs when the hold-up horses launch their challenges. The lack of pace pressure strongly favours hold-up performers who can produce a finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Favours Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Global Hideaway sets steady fractions without serious challenge
scenarios.body: The moderate early pace allows hold-up horses to conserve energy and time their runs perfectly from off the bridle. Prettylady, Phantom Gold and Caspada benefit most from this patient tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Apply Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Collanisi or Paragon decide to press Global Hideaway early
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field and creates a more honest gallop that suits horses with tactical speed. This scenario plays into the hands of the prominent runners who can dictate from forward positions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Global Hideaway Dominates Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If the leader kicks clear turning for home unopposed
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader builds an unassailable advantage that the closers cannot peg back despite their finishing efforts. Global Hideaway's front-running style proves perfectly suited to the lack of early pressure.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Into Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes walking-pace slow
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint from the final 2 furlongs where only the sharpest finishers can quicken decisively. This suits horses with proven turn of foot over those relying on stamina.

Paragon in first-time cheekpieces could show improved focus if settling better than recent Market Rasen run
Caspada's odds-defying Chepstow second suggests Donald McCain has found the key to unlocking improvement

races.name: Free Racenight Thursday 18th June Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Callin Baton Rouge
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited to this honest pace scenario with 21 days since last run ideal for peak fitness
runners_data.comment: Not quite at best this year but has dropped another 2lb since last month's third
runners_data.spotlight: Not quite at her best this year but has dropped another 2lb since last month's respectable third at Huntingdon (2m, good to firm) and this move back up in trip won't be a problem; probably won't be far away.

runners_data.name: William Of York
runners_data.note: Prominent style but poor completion rate over fences raises stamina doubts despite respectable last hurdle run
runners_data.comment: Regressive 10yo; latest run stopped the rot but he needs to build on that effort here
runners_data.spotlight: Regressive 10yo who has poor completion rate over fences since returning from layoff in November; stopped the rot with fairly respectable hurdle run last month but needs to build on that performance here; swaps visor for refitted cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Achille Des Rocs
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 65-day break after disappointing chase comeback but has proven hurdle ability
runners_data.comment: Dual hurdle winner in 2024; returned from layoff with disappointing chase run in April
runners_data.spotlight: Dual hurdle winner (2m/2m3f, good) towards end of 2024; not yet fully exposed but returned from one-year absence with disappointing chase run in April and needs to get career back on track.

runners_data.name: Golden Glance
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse out of form since December but wind operation may have addressed her issues
runners_data.comment: Out of form since returning from long absence in December; needs to turn a corner
runners_data.spotlight: Out of form since returning from long absence in December, albeit her seventh of eight at Aintree (2m4f, good; first run after wind op) last month was arguably more encouraging than bare form suggests; others have more pressing claims.

runners_data.name: Fighting Falcon
runners_data.note: Sole pace-setter with tendency to fade in finish but recent Uttoxeter win suggests improved stamina
runners_data.comment: Made winning stable debut when back under rules last month and remains lightly raced
runners_data.spotlight: Low-mileage 5yo who made winning stable debut when back under rules at Uttoxeter (2m4f, good; first-time cheekpieces) last month; drew well clear of the others with the runner-up there and could still be well treated after a 6lb rise.

runners_data.name: Gone In Sixty
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner on attractive mark at 145lbs despite recent fall, trip extension should suit
runners_data.comment: Fell at Fakenham recently but remains on a good mark and conditions here will suit
runners_data.spotlight: Returned from break with low-key chase run last month and fell mid-race when back over hurdles nine days ago but remains on a good mark and will be suited by today's trip/ground; can't be ruled out.

runners_data.name: Royal Rhythm
runners_data.note: Prominent style but winless since December 2023 though narrow Worcester defeat shows retained ability
runners_data.comment: Returned from break with satisfactory run last month; contender if that brought him on
runners_data.spotlight: Without a win since December 2023 but lost out only by a nose at Worcester (2m4f, good) last summer and returned from break with satisfactory run at Fontwell last month; contender if that recent outing brought him on.

runners_data.name: Ruler Legend
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in excellent recent form with two Market Rasen wins and solid recent second
runners_data.comment: Won twice at Market Rasen in April and his recent second there was another good effort
runners_data.spotlight: Ended last season in excellent form, winning twice at Market Rasen (2m/2m2f, good), and his second at Market Rasen (2m, good) 12 days ago was another good effort; should be fine over this longer trip; respected.

races.paceDynamic: Fighting Falcon is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the start in this small field. With William Of York, Achille Des Rocs, Royal Rhythm and Ruler Legend all preferring prominent positions, there should be reasonable pace behind the leader but nothing frantic. The sustained gallop over this staying trip will create a proper test of stamina, with the race likely decided by who stays strongest in the final half-mile rather than any dramatic pace collapse. This setup strongly favours hold-up horses who can finish with one sustained run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners fail to sustain their effort over this staying trip
scenarios.body: The pace will be honest but not destructive, allowing closers to time their challenges perfectly and overwhelm the early leaders in the final furlong. Callin Baton Rouge and Gone In Sixty benefit most from their patient tactics and superior finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners can settle better than usual and conserve energy
scenarios.body: The honest pace will suit a horse like Ruler Legend or Achille Des Rocs who can track the leader without over-racing and kick clear when Fighting Falcon weakens. Their class tells in a sustained battle from the last fence.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Fighting Falcon Stays Strong
scenarios.trigger: If the 5-year-old's stamina reserves prove deeper than his profile suggests
scenarios.body: The leader will maintain his advantage throughout, with the chasing pack unable to reel him in despite the honest pace. His recent Uttoxeter win suggests improved staying power that could surprise at bigger odds.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners go too fast early trying to pressure Fighting Falcon
scenarios.body: The race will become a sprint from the last fence, suiting any horse with a turn of foot regardless of position. This creates opportunities for outsiders who get the right split-second timing in a bunched finish.

watchPoints.text: Fighting Falcon's early fractions will determine if he can sustain his kick or sets up the race for closers
Achille Des Rocs returning from 65-day absence after disappointing chase run needs close monitoring for fitness

William Of York's poor fence completion rate suggests stamina limitations that could surface over this trip
Callin Baton Rouge dropping further in grade after respectable Huntingdon third suggests connections expect improvement

races.name: Celebrate With Sponsorship At Southwell Racecourse Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Artiste d'Ainay
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but 21 days off and needs to prove hurdles form translates from point-to-point success
runners_data.comment: Point winner this spring; just a respectable fifth when back over hurdles last month
runners_data.spotlight: Easily made all in a point in April but was just a respectable fifth over hurdles at Hexham (2m7f, good) for new connections last month and needs to build on that performance here.

runners_data.name: Copper Beach
runners_data.note: Sharp prominent style with tongue-tie working well in recent seconds, trip extension should suit
runners_data.comment: Second twice last month (2m4f/2m3f), after a layoff, and this longer trip should suit
runners_data.spotlight: Came from off the pace to take second twice last month (2m4f/2m3f, good; tongue-tie added), after a long layoff, and is likely to be suited by this move back up in trip; must be considered.

runners_data.name: Danger Nap
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front runner with cheekpieces working last time, unexposed 5yo with stamina to prove
runners_data.comment: Clear second when upped to 3m1f for last month's handicap debut; has more to offer
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed 5yo who was clear second when upped to 3m1f and fitted with first-time cheekpieces for last month's handicap debut at Warwick (good); could still have more to offer; high on the list.

runners_data.name: Ikigai Star
runners_data.note: Prominent racer but pulled up last time raises questions about stamina for this extended trip
runners_data.comment: Ran okay two starts ago but pulled up since and has stamina to prove today
runners_data.spotlight: Ran okay when third of five at Fontwell (2m1f, good to soft) in April but was pulled up on latest outing, and his Flat pedigree raises doubts about the suitability of this new trip; swaps cheekpieces for refitted visor.

runners_data.name: East Eagle
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited, 9-length Stratford winner shows he thrives over staying trips
runners_data.comment: Good winner at Stratford in April but seemingly a shade too high in the weights now
runners_data.spotlight: Showed career-best form when scoring by 9l at Stratford (3m2f, good) in April and also has a C&D success on his CV but was unable to land a telling blow on his two starts at Hexham last month and needs to kick on again to overcome current mark.

runners_data.name: Iamcelestialgift
runners_data.note: Prominent style but 151 days off and struggled in handicaps, major fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: Struggled in first two handicaps; returns from five-month break here
runners_data.spotlight: Won on hurdling debut in April 2025 (2m3f) but struggled in both handicaps last season (3m/2m5f); returns from five-month break with a lot to prove.

runners_data.name: Indian Sunbird
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with proven C&D form and good ground specialist, entitled to strip fitter
runners_data.comment: Won twice (once over C&D) last year but may find others in this field better handicapped
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice last year on good ground (once over C&D) and is entitled to have benefited from last month's reappearance run but may find others in this field better handicapped.

runners_data.name: Getaway Glory
runners_data.note: Hold-up style fits but completely out of form and first-time visor adds unknown element
runners_data.comment: Out of form since returning from long absence; headgear switched; revival needed
runners_data.spotlight: Out of form (mainly over fences) since returning from long absence in January (had wind op before latest run); swaps cheekpieces for first-time visor and has tongue-tie refitted; revival needed.

runners_data.name: Fairly Fulling
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who found his level over hurdles, pulled up last time over shorter trip
runners_data.comment: 2m4f winner in March; pulled up over 2m since; hard to predict over this new trip
runners_data.spotlight: Came good over hurdles at 14th attempt, with clear success at Newcastle (2m4f, good to soft) in March, but ran poorly when dropped back to 2m last month and it's hard to know what to expect from him on first attempt at 3m under rules.

runners_data.name: Can U Feel It

runners_data.comment: Placed over 2m4f at Fakenham last month and open to more improvement over this trip
runners_data.spotlight: 0-6 over hurdles but put in good front-running shift when third at Fakenham (2m4f, good; first-time tongue-tie) last month and is open to more improvement over this longer trip.

runners_data.name: L'Air du Large
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse but 169 days off and struggled in previous handicaps, huge fitness ask

runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed after only five hurdle runs but struggled in first two handicaps (2m/2m3f; cheekpieces added last time); upped in trip again for first run since December; considered only if lively in the betting.

runners_data.name: Stripe Of Honour
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran with proven C&D form but 250 days off creates massive fitness doubt

runners_data.name: Porridge

runners_data.spotlight: 0-14 over hurdles; excelled herself when fourth at huge odds in 2m3f Fontwell maiden in April but, having been hiked up the weights, was soundly beaten in both subsequent handicaps (2m5f/2m7f).

races.paceDynamic: Danger Nap will set the pace as the only confirmed front runner, likely joined by prominent racers Copper Beach, Artiste d'Ainay, and Ikigai Star in the early stages. The sustainable pace over this extended 3m½f trip will suit those who can travel kindly in the first half before mounting challenges. With most of the field preferring to hold up or come from midfield positions, the race will develop into a stamina test from 3f out. This tactical setup strongly favours hold-up horses who can finish with a sustained gallop, as they'll benefit from the solid pace and have fewer rivals to beat from similar positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace holds up and the prominent horses tire from 3f out
scenarios.body: The patient tactics of East Eagle, Indian Sunbird, and Can U Feel It will be perfectly suited as they pick off tiring leaders in the final furlong. Their stamina reserves and tactical positioning allow them to sweep past the pace-setters.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the early pace angles proves tougher than expected
scenarios.body: Copper Beach or Danger Nap could use their early positioning to steal a march, with their recent form suggesting they can sustain a gallop better than usual. The hold-up horses may leave their runs too late over this stamina-sapping distance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Favours Finishers
scenarios.trigger: If Danger Nap goes too slowly early and kicks clear late
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where the strongest stayers with pace can unleash telling bursts. Indian Sunbird and East Eagle would be perfectly placed to deliver knockout blows in a tactical affair.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Package Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the market leaders fail to handle the trip or going
scenarios.body: Stripe Of Honour's C&D win or Fairly Fulling's improved hurdles form could see them outrun expectations. Their lower weights and proven stamina could prove decisive if the pace collapses.

Indian Sunbird and East Eagle being held up too far back given their proven stamina advantages

Any of the long-absent horses like Stripe Of Honour or L'Air du Large showing early signs of rustiness
